subject: Re: HelixCloud MSA — defense control & insurance offset proposal
messages:
From: Tom Walters <twalters@helixcloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Sue Harper <sue.harper@helixcloud.com>, HelixCloud Legal <legal@helixcloud.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HelixCloud MSA — IP indemnity and defense control

Grace —

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA. Our legal team flagged the IP indemnity (Section 9) as currently broader than we can accept for a procurement deal of this size. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Defense control — HelixCloud typically insists on the right to control the defense of third-party IP claims against our customers, with Redwood required to cooperate and cover defense costs where appropriate.

2) Insurance offset — we need explicit language that insurance proceeds reduce Redwood's indemnity exposure (we call this an insurance offset).

I've attached a short redline (HCL-Redline-1.docx) with our preferred language and a couple of carveouts (OSS, customer-uploaded content). Can Kimberly or your counsel take a look and let us know whether Redwood can accept a hybrid where HelixCloud controls defense but Redwood has the option to step in and take over subject to cooperation and settlement approval thresholds?

We'd like to avoid protracted back-and-forth if possible — happy to do a short legal-only call this week.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Walters
Head of Procurement, Cloud Partnerships
HelixCloud
Phone: +1 415 555 0172

Subject: Re: HelixCloud MSA — IP indemnity and defense control

Tom —

Appreciate the clear framing and the redline. Looping in Kimberly (legal), Ben (account lead) and Logan (ops) so we can propose a practical compromise.

Short summary of Redwood’s posture: we want to avoid blanket acceptance of defense control where claim handling could materially impact our warranty or product roadmap. That said, we can do a hybrid approach that preserves HelixCloud’s operational choice while protecting Redwood from unilateral settlements that create ongoing obligations. 

Proposed compromise we are attaching: RWI-Redline-v2.docx — key points:
- HelixCloud gets initial right to defend.
- Redwood may elect to assume defense within 30 days of notice if it reimburses documented defense costs to date and obtains reasonable cooperation.
- Settlements that impose obligations other than money damages (e.g., product changes, takedown obligations) require joint written approval if above $100,000.
- Insurance offset language that uses net recoveries after HelixCloud’s reasonable costs (we proposed a waterfall).
- Explicit carveouts for OSS and customer-supplied code (we accept narrower carveouts tied to upstream OSS licenses).

Logan — can you prepare a short evidence-staging template (what we need if a claim arises) so we can show HelixCloud we can meet custody/forensics requests without risking data leakage? I’ve attached an example spreadsheet (evidence-staging-template.xlsx) for discussion.

Tom — can you confirm HelixCloud’s usual notice window (you suggested 10 business days in your redline) and whether you can share your insurer name / coverage limit (pdf ok)? That will help Kimberly calibrate the insurance-offset language.

If this looks broadly acceptable, can we book a 30-minute call (legal-only) tomorrow or Tuesday?

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-10T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelixCloud MSA — IP indemnity and defense control

Tom / team —

Thanks for the redline and Grace for the draft compromise. A few tactical points from legal that should shorten negotiation: 

1) Hybrid defense control — we can accept HelixCloud’s initial control with Redwood right to assume under the conditions in RWI-Redline-v2, but we need clearer language around: (a) documentation of defense costs for reimbursement; (b) Redwood’s ability to appoint counsel of record if it takes over; and (c) a mechanism to resolve disputes about whether a settlement requires joint approval (we propose binding arbitration for settlement disputes > $250k).

2) Insurance offset — we will accept an insurance offset but propose Redwood’s indemnity is reduced by net proceeds actually collected by the claimant or HelixCloud after reasonable claims-handling expenses. Please confirm insurer details so we can draft the offset waterfall.

3) OSS/customer-content carveouts — we can accept targeted carveouts but want HelixCloud to confirm whether your customer agreements include indemnities of their own (so we avoid gap).

4) Evidence custody & privilege — Redwood needs a short chain-of-custody and privilege-protection protocol before we can hand over internal logs or model snapshots. Logan, please confirm the retention window for the logs we’d need to preserve and the redaction approach for customer PII.

If Tom can upload the insurance schedule and confirm the notice window, I’ll prepare a short redline (tracked) that we can circulate. If HelixCloud would prefer, we can also do a 30-minute counsel-to-counsel call — happy to host.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: none in-line

Kimberly / Grace —

Thanks for the constructive approach. A couple points to move us forward: 

- HelixCloud confirms a 10 business-day notice window is our ask, but we can accept 15 business days if Redwood needs a slightly longer intake period.

- Attached is our insurance schedule (Helix-insurance-dec2025.pdf). Our primary insurer is NorthernGate Insurance; general aggregate is $5M.

- On OSS and customer-supplied content: we can accept narrow carveouts for claims that arise solely from OSS licensed dependencies where Redwood has not modified the OSS and where the claimant’s claim is based on upstream license terms. For customer-uploaded content, we propose Redwood remains responsible if the content routed through Redwood’s runtime created the infringing output.

- Regarding settlements: HelixCloud is comfortable with a joint-approval threshold. We’d prefer the $100k threshold be negotiable based on deal size (propose $100k for deals under $1M TCV, escalate for larger deals).

We’re fine with a counsel-to-counsel call — available Tue Jul 13 11am PT or Wed Jul 14 10am PT.

Tom

Thanks — that insurance schedule helps. Quick summary and next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

1) Counsel sync: Wed Jul 14, 10:00am PT — Kimberly and Helix legal to discuss the proposed RWI-Redline-v2 and the insurance offset waterfall. Can you confirm the meeting invite and preferred dial-in?

2) Action owners:
- Ben (sales) will draft a Mutual Action Plan for procurement signoff and to surface whether deal-level threshold adjustments make sense.
- Logan (ops) will finalize the evidence-staging template and include the log retention and redaction notes Kimberly requested.
- Kimberly will produce a short tracked redline that incorporates the hybrid defense-control language and an insurance-offset clause tied to the uploaded schedule; she will also add a dispute mechanism for settlements over $250k.

3) OSS carveouts and customer-content definitions — Tom, please have your legal ops confirm whether your customers’ standard agreements include upstream indemnities; if you can share an exemplar customer T&Cs that would save time.

If we get counsel alignment on Wednesday, Ben and I will push the commercial terms into the order form and get procurement in both orgs aligned on the settlement threshold logic.

Appreciate the constructive tone here — looks like we can get to a pragmatic compromise.

Best,
